name: Malta
title: Malta Ship Thickness Measurement | UTM for Malta-Flag Fleet
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Malta at Grand Harbour, Marsaxlokk and offshore anchorages: renewal survey gauging, CAP support and scrubber piping.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement in Malta: Grand Harbour, Marsaxlokk and Offshore
intro: Malta sits on the main east–west Mediterranean route and administers Europe's largest ship register, so ships of every type pass its ports, drydocks and offshore bunkering areas. Whether a ship is in drydock at Grand Harbour, working cargo at the Malta Freeport or lying at anchor off the south-east coast between voyages, Atlantis NDT can fly a thickness measurement team in from India and gauge it within the window the owner has.

highlights.p: Palumbo Malta Shipyard in the historic dock area at Cospicua docks cruise ships, tankers, bulk carriers and offshore units, so renewal surveys and full hull gauging are routinely carried out on the island.
Ships calling at the offshore anchorages, including Hurd's Bank, for fuel, stores or orders can be gauged by launch while they wait, without diverting to a port or booking a berth.
Many ship managers and owners operate from Malta because of its flag, so decisions about gauging ships trading worldwide are often taken on the island, close to the yard and the surveyors.

port.h: Malta's ports, anchorages and the ships that use them
p: Malta's maritime activity is spread across two main ports and the sea around them. Grand Harbour, between Valletta and the Three Cities, holds the Valletta Cruise Port and the island's ship-repair yard, Palumbo Malta Shipyard, in the historic dock area at Cospicua. Marsaxlokk, in the south-east, is home to the Malta Freeport container transhipment terminal at Birżebbuġa and to oil storage and bulk terminals. Offshore, designated anchorage and bunkering areas, including Hurd's Bank, serve ships calling only for fuel, stores, crew changes or orders, and make Malta a well-used bunkering location on the central Mediterranean route.

That mix creates a broad inspection demand. The shipyard docks cruise ships, ferries, tankers, bulk carriers and offshore units for repair and refit, and its dockings are where renewal surveys and full hull gauging take place. The Freeport's transhipment calls bring large container ships whose scrubber piping and ballast tanks can be gauged during the cargo exchange. The offshore anchorages bring something less common: ships with no berth booking at all, lying at anchor for a day or two for bunkers or orders, which a superintendent can use for pre-purchase, on-hire, off-hire or close-out gauging without diverting the ship into port. On an island this size, all three are within a short distance of each other.

The Malta flag adds another layer. Transport Malta's Merchant Shipping Directorate administers Europe's largest ship register, and Malta-flagged ships trade worldwide, with statutory surveys carried out by the classification societies that Malta authorises as recognised organisations. Many ship-management and owning companies are established on the island because of the flag, so technical decisions for ships trading far from the Mediterranean are often made in Malta. For those managers, a Malta mobilisation can also be the starting point for gauging a fleet ship calling elsewhere in the central Mediterranean, in Sicily or southern Italy.

facilities.h: Where thickness gauging happens around Malta
p: Docking work centres on the Grand Harbour drydock complex at Palumbo Malta Shipyard, where graving docks of different sizes take ships from ferries and offshore vessels up to large cruise ships and tankers. A docking gives the full range of access: bottom shell and sea chests in the dock, cargo and ballast tanks once gas-freed and ventilated, and staging for close-up survey in the larger spaces. Cruise lines use the yard for refurbishments, which bring scrubber and exhaust system work alongside hull items, and the gauging is sequenced around the yard's own trades.

Outside the yard, Marsaxlokk handles the Freeport's container ships and the tankers and bulk carriers using its oil and bulk terminals, with gauging done alongside under each terminal's safety rules. The Valletta cruise berths give turnaround-day access. Thickness gauging at anchor, at Hurd's Bank or the other designated areas, is done from a launch arranged through the agent and depends on the weather: these areas are exposed, and a sea state that is fine for bunkering may still rule out safe boarding with equipment. Where conditions are marginal, the work can move to a more sheltered spot or to the ship's next call.
list: Palumbo Malta Shipyard, Grand Harbour — drydock gauging of bottom shell, sea chests and tanks, with close-up survey support during repairs, refits and renewal surveys
Valletta Cruise Port — turnarounds in Grand Harbour, giving a day for exhaust gas cleaning pipework and items from the previous survey
Malta Freeport, Birżebbuġa — transhipment calls on large container ships, used for ballast tank close-out readings and scrubber discharge line checks
Oil and bulk terminals at Marsaxlokk — gauging of deck, deck piping and accessible ballast tanks on tankers and bulk carriers within the cargo window
Hurd's Bank and the designated offshore anchorages — pre-purchase, on-hire, off-hire and close-out gauging by launch while ships bunker or wait for orders

context.h: Flag, port state control and emissions context in Malta
p: Malta is a member of both the Paris MoU and the Mediterranean MoU, and as an EU state applies the EU port state control regime to foreign ships in its ports. For Malta-flagged ships the flag state relies on recognised organisations for statutory surveys, and the class society concerned sets the thickness measurement requirements for each survey under IACS UR Z7 and, for ESP ships, the UR Z10 series. Under UR Z17 those measurements must be taken by a firm holding approval from that society, so managers confirm the approval position for the ship's class before booking any gauging that will be credited to a survey.

Malta's waters have been inside the Mediterranean SOx ECA since 1 May 2025, so the island's bunker suppliers now serve ships that must burn 0.10% sulphur fuel in the central Mediterranean unless they carry a scrubber delivering the equivalent. Ships that rely on scrubbers run them throughout these waters, and their wash-water and overboard piping is a frequent target when ships stop for bunkers. EU ETS, which has covered shipping since 2024, and FuelEU Maritime, since 2025, apply to Malta port calls and are followed closely by the island's ship managers, including those running tanker and bulk carrier fleets, where steel condition shapes the decision to keep or sell a ship.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Malta
jobs.p: Malta jobs range from full docking programmes at Grand Harbour to a few hours on a ship at anchor between bunkering and sailing. What they share is the island's central position: ships come to Malta for fuel, repair or transhipment, and a superintendent can use that stop for gauging without adding a port call. We plan each job around the docking, the cargo window or the bunkering schedule.
list: Renewal survey gauging on a bulk carrier in a Grand Harbour drydock, covering cargo hold and ballast tank structure for its third renewal survey under the ESP regime
CAP thickness measurement support on an older tanker at the shipyard, gauging cargo and ballast tanks after gas-freeing ahead of the owner's CAP inspection
Wall-thickness survey of a cruise ship's scrubber discharge lines and shell outlets during a refurbishment at Palumbo Malta Shipyard, with the outlets gauged while the ship is dry
Off-hire condition gauging on a tanker at anchor off Malta while it bunkers, documenting deck and accessible ballast tank condition at the end of a charter
Ballast tank and hatch cover gauging on a container ship during a transhipment call at the Malta Freeport, closing out items from its last annual survey

logistics: Malta International Airport at Luqa has direct European connections and lies close to both Grand Harbour and Marsaxlokk, so equipment reaches either port quickly by road. The shipyard and the terminals require ISPS passes arranged through the agent or the yard, and the agent books launches for ships at anchor, subject to weather. Malta belongs to the Schengen area, and the team from India enters on Schengen visas. Shipyard dockings are planned well in advance, which suits visa timing; anchorage work tied to a bunkering stop is best raised as soon as the ship's voyage plan includes Malta.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship at anchor off Malta during bunkering?
faqs.a: Yes, when the weather allows safe boarding with equipment. Deck plating, deck piping and any tank the crew makes safe for entry can be measured while the ship bunkers or waits for orders. The offshore areas are exposed, so we keep the plan flexible and agree priorities with the superintendent in case the window shortens.

faqs.q: Is a Malta-flag ship gauged differently from other ships?
faqs.a: No. The flag does not change the measurement work: the classification society acting as the ship's recognised organisation sets the thickness measurement requirements for each survey under the IACS rules. What the Malta flag does mean is that the manager, the yard and the attending surveyor are often all on the island during a Grand Harbour docking, which keeps scoping decisions quick.

faqs.q: Can ship inspection in Malta be combined with work in Sicily or southern Italy?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Sicily is a short flight or ferry crossing away, and a Schengen visa covers both Malta and Italy. If an owner has a docking in Malta and another fleet ship calling in Sicily or at Naples, we can sequence both jobs within one mobilisation and report them separately.

faqs.q: When should we book gauging for a Grand Harbour drydock?
faqs.a: As soon as the docking slot is confirmed. That gives time for visas and lets us plan the gauging sequence with the yard, so that readings are taken before blasting and in time for steel renewal decisions. For CAP or renewal surveys on ESP ships, early booking also allows the tank programme to be agreed with the surveyor in advance.
